title: PMP: Pattern Morphing-based Memory Partitioning in High-Level Synthesis
problem: Memory partitioning in high-level synthesis is constrained by fixed access pattern shapes, leading to sub-optimal bank numbers or excessive address generation overhead. Previous hyperplane-based methods cannot flexibly adapt to varying data access patterns.
motivation: Reducing memory access conflicts and improving FPGA resource utilization through more effective memory partitioning strategies in automated hardware synthesis.
method: PMP proposes a pattern-morphing approach that flexibly transforms memory access patterns using reduced hyperplane families to achieve minimal bank numbers. An integer linear programming (ILP) problem is formulated to minimize data padding overhead during pattern morphing, replacing the rigid pattern constraints of prior hyperplane-based methods.
key_novelty: Pattern morphing combined with ILP formulation enables flexible memory partitioning that achieves optimal bank counts independent of input access pattern shapes.
contributions: Pattern morphing-based memory partitioning technique for HLS
ILP formulation to minimize data padding overhead
Optimal partition factor determination without pattern shape restrictions
Average 22% LUT, 21% FlipFlop, 10% DSP, and 40% memory overhead reduction versus prior methods
primary_theme: Memory partitioning optimization for FPGA synthesis
